headline: UK Graduate Visa Requirements in 2026
metaDescription: UK Graduate visa requirements for 2026: who can apply, how long it lasts, the £937 fee plus health surcharge, and how to switch to a Skilled Worker visa.

sections.content:
The Graduate visa is a post-study work visa for international students who have completed an eligible UK degree while holding a Student visa. It lets graduates live and work in the UK without needing a job offer or a sponsor, which makes it one of the most flexible routes after graduation.

Holders can work in almost any job, be self-employed, or look for work while living in the UK. There is no minimum salary requirement and no restriction on the type of work, apart from a few roles such as professional sportsperson. It is designed as a bridge between study and longer-term work routes.
sections.title: What is the UK Graduate visa?

sections.content:
To qualify, you must have completed an eligible course at a UK higher education provider with a track record of compliance, and your university must have confirmed your successful completion to the Home Office. You must apply from inside the UK, before your current Student permission expires.

For longer courses, you must have studied in the UK for at least 12 months. You cannot apply from outside the UK, and you cannot apply if your Student visa has already expired, so timing the application around your course end date matters.
sections.title: Who can apply and when

sections.content:
The length of the Graduate visa depends on when you apply. Applications made on or before 31 December 2026 are granted for two years, or three years for PhD and other doctoral graduates. Applications made on or after 1 January 2027 are granted for 18 months instead, with PhD graduates still receiving three years.

This change makes the end of 2026 an important cut-off for graduates finishing their courses around that time. The visa cannot be extended, so anyone who wants to stay longer must switch to another route before it expires.

The application fee is £937, plus the Immigration Health Surcharge of £1,035 per year. For a two-year visa, the total cost is around £3,007. You pay the full surcharge upfront when you apply, and the fee is the same whether you apply for two years or 18 months.

The Graduate visa is not a route to settlement, and time spent on it does not count directly towards indefinite leave to remain. Most graduates who want to stay switch to a Skilled Worker visa, which requires a job offer from a licensed sponsor meeting the salary and skill thresholds in force at the time.
